reason: A petioluliform base narrows into a short stalk, like a petiolule. This is the 'abruptly narrowed at the base into a stalk-like part' of FLOPO clawed.
A polyembryonic seed has more than one embryo ('seed with numerous embryos'). It is a count of plant embryo (PO_0009009) per seed greater than one, not a quality of the seed.

target: new: conjunction of two values in one word
reason: Both values hold together: the margin is fringed with hairs (ciliated, PATO_0001408) and those hairs are minute (puberulous, FLOPO:0991049). It is not a transition between two values, and both parts already have terms.
Simultaneous flowers open at the same time. That is synchronous, a quality of the process (anthesis), so it inheres in the flowering rather than in the flower itself.

'Suffused with red' is a red tinge over the ground colour, like the existing composite 'white tinged with pink'. The red component is PATO red. Its location ('at base', 'along the margin') goes into the region slot.
'Leaf blade widest proximal to middle' is the 'broadest below the middle, towards the base' of the FLOPO ovate definition. The rule applies only when followed by 'to middle'.
It is unclear whether this means 'not dilated' or that some unnamed swellings are absent. One example ('or dilations') is a transcription fragment.
'Held close to the stamens / to the rachis' is appressed (FLOPO:0991064) relative to a named second part. FLOPO appressed itself requires the structure the bearer lies against.
An indented fruit or achene apex is notched at the tip, which is PATO emarginate. 'Not indented' negates it.

Vespertine flowers open in the evening and stay open into the night. PATO nocturnal (a process happening during the hours of darkness) covers this, applied to anthesis. The narrower 'evening' sense is lost.

label: pseudoterminal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's appearing to terminate a shoot while arising from the axil of its uppermost leaf, the shoot apex being reduced or arrested.
reason: A real botanical position, between FLOPO axillary (FLOPO:0991000) and PATO terminal (PATO_0002476) and neither of them. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991000 axillary.
A fragment of 'base not or slightly narrowed' / 'not or shortly clawed'. The quality is the following word, negated.
A 3-D fruit broadest near its top is broadest above the middle with the narrow end at the base, which is FLOPO obovoid.

label: finger-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongate, more or less cylindrical and blunt at the tip, like a finger.
reason: There is no PATO term: PATO_0001980 digitate means palmately compound, not finger-shaped. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991040 claw-shaped. The bearers are mostly projections or cells, which need their organ.

target: new: part bearing its own quality (has part some (bract PO_0009055 and has characteristic leaf-like PATO_0002457))
reason: The quality belongs to the bracts of the inflorescence or peduncle, which are leaf-like. It is not a quality of the axis itself.
FLOPO lyrate is defined as pinnately lobed or divided with a large terminal lobe and smaller lobes towards the base, which is exactly 'lyrately pinnatifid'.
Costate means ribbed and 'multi-' gives no number, so the value is FLOPO ribbed.
Paniculiform is a listed synonym of FLOPO panicle-like. 'Narrowly' is a degree word for the outline and adds no separate quality.
Pachycaul means having a disproportionately thick stem or trunk. Annotate the stem (PO_0009047) with increased thickness (exact synonym: stout), even when the source says 'whole plant'.
A spelling variant of scale-like. In 'scalelike hairy' the bearer is the hairs (trichome).

target: new: conjunction of two values in one word
reason: Both values hold together: spongy (PATO_0001480) and increased thickness (PATO_0000591). Both terms exist.
'Sub-' here means 'nearly' (like suborbicular): approximately centered (PATO_0002268).
Directed obliquely upward is ascending. The opposite, FLOPO descending, is defined as its sibling.
The previous review mapped 'narrowed' to PATO tapered. 'Hardly narrowed' (base hardly narrowed) means practically not tapered.
A root or caudex with several crowns (stem bases) is a count of parts greater than one. PO has no root crown class, so this cannot be annotated until a bearer exists.
Not clearly visible, the same reading as 'obscure' and 'indistinct' in the previous review.
Negates PATO retuse (a rounded end with a depressed centre). It applies to teeth and scales.
Styles and phyllary tips curving outward, away from the axis, are recurved in the botanical sense (curved backward). PATO has no 'curved outward'.
A spicate panicle (mostly grasses) is a contracted panicle whose overall form resembles a spike. The inflorescence is a panicle with a spike-like form, not a transition between two values.
Capitula or spikelets arranged in a spike make up a spike-like compound inflorescence. The value inheres in the inflorescence that holds them, not in each spikelet.
